1	# BOLT
2	
3	BOLT is a post-link optimizer developed to speed up large applications.
4	It achieves the improvements by optimizing application's code layout based on
5	execution profile gathered by sampling profiler, such as Linux `perf` tool.
6	An overview of the ideas implemented in BOLT along with a discussion of its
7	potential and current results is available in
8	[CGO'19 paper](https://research.fb.com/publications/bolt-a-practical-binary-optimizer-for-data-centers-and-beyond/).
9	
10	## Input Binary Requirements
11	
12	BOLT operates on X86-64 and AArch64 ELF binaries. At the minimum, the binaries
13	should have an unstripped symbol table, and, to get maximum performance gains,
14	they should be linked with relocations (`--emit-relocs` or `-q` linker flag).
15	
16	BOLT disassembles functions and reconstructs the control flow graph (CFG)
17	before it runs optimizations. Since this is a nontrivial task,
18	especially when indirect branches are present, we rely on certain heuristics
19	to accomplish it. These heuristics have been tested on a code generated with
20	Clang and GCC compilers. The main requirement for C/C++ code is not to rely
21	on code layout properties, such as function pointer deltas.
22	Assembly code can be processed too. Requirements for it include a clear
23	separation of code and data, with data objects being placed into data
24	sections/segments. If indirect jumps are used for intra-function control
25	transfer (e.g., jump tables), the code patterns should be matching those
26	generated by Clang/GCC.
27	
28	NOTE: BOLT is currently incompatible with the `-freorder-blocks-and-partition`
29	compiler option. Since GCC8 enables this option by default, you have to
30	explicitly disable it by adding `-fno-reorder-blocks-and-partition` flag if
31	you are compiling with GCC8 or above.
32	
33	PIE and .so support has been added recently. Please report bugs if you
34	encounter any issues.
35	
36	## Installation
37	
38	### Docker Image
39	
40	You can build and use the docker image containing BOLT using our [docker file](utils/docker/Dockerfile).
41	Alternatively, you can build BOLT manually using the steps below.
42	
43	### Manual Build
44	
45	BOLT heavily uses LLVM libraries, and by design, it is built as one of LLVM
46	tools. The build process is not much different from a regular LLVM build.
47	The following instructions are assuming that you are running under Linux.
48	
49	Start with cloning LLVM repo:
50	
51	```
52	> git clone https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git
53	> mkdir build
54	> cd build
55	> cmake -G Ninja ../llvm-project/llvm -DLLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="X86;AArch64" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS="bolt"
56	> ninja bolt
57	```
58	
59	`llvm-bolt` will be available under `bin/`. Add this directory to your path to
60	ensure the rest of the commands in this tutorial work.
61	
62	### Testing changes during development
63	
64	During development, it is recommended to run both the in-tree tests (under
65	[bolt/test](./test)) and the out-of-tree tests, which are currently hosted in
66	the following repositories:
67	- [rafaelauler/bolt-tests](https://github.com/rafaelauler/bolt-tests): covers both X86 and AArch64 binaries tests
68	- [arm/large-bolt-tests](https://github.com/arm/large-bolt-tests): additional AArch64 binaries
69	
70	
71	Below are sample instructions to run all test suites. You may need to define
72	additional CMake variables. The [docker-tests/Dockerfile ](./utils/docker-tests/Dockerfile)
73	is provided which is another route to get a known good testing environment.
74	
75	```bash
76	git clone https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git
77	git clone https://github.com/rafaelauler/bolt-tests
78	git clone https://github.com/arm/large-bolt-tests.git
79	
80	mkdir build
81	cmake -G Ninja -S llvm-project/llvm -B build \
82	       -DLLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="AArch64;X86" \
83	       -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
84	       -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON \
85	       -DLLVM_BUILD_TOOLS=ON \
86	       -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON \
87	       -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS="clang;bolt;lld" \
88	       -DLLVM_USE_LINKER=lld \
89	       -DLLVM_CCACHE_BUILD=ON \
90	       -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_PROJECTS="bolttests;bolttests-arm" \
91	       -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_BOLTTESTS_SOURCE_DIR="$(pwd)/bolt-tests"
92	       -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_BOLTTESTS_ARM_SOURCE_DIR="$(pwd)/large-bolt-tests"
93	
94	
95	ninja -C build check-bolt check-large-bolt check-large-bolt-arm
96	```
97	
98	## Optimizing BOLT's Performance
99	
100	BOLT runs many internal passes in parallel. If you foresee heavy usage of
101	BOLT, you can improve the processing time by linking against one of memory
102	allocation libraries with good support for concurrency. E.g. to use jemalloc:
103	
104	```
105	> sudo yum install jemalloc-devel
106	> LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libjemalloc.so llvm-bolt ....
107	```
108	Or if you rather use tcmalloc:
109	```
110	> sudo yum install gperftools-devel
111	> LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libtcmalloc_minimal.so llvm-bolt ....
112	```
113	
114	## Usage
115	
116	For a complete practical guide of using BOLT see [Optimizing Clang with BOLT](docs/OptimizingClang.md).
117	
118	### Step 0
119	
120	In order to allow BOLT to re-arrange functions (in addition to re-arranging
121	code within functions) in your program, it needs a little help from the linker.
122	Add `--emit-relocs` to the final link step of your application. You can verify
123	the presence of relocations by checking for `.rela.text` section in the binary.
124	BOLT will also report if it detects relocations while processing the binary.
125	
126	### Step 1: Collect Profile
127	
128	This step is different for different kinds of executables. If you can invoke
129	your program to run on a representative input from a command line, then check
130	**For Applications** section below. If your program typically runs as a
131	server/service, then skip to **For Services** section.
132	
133	The version of `perf` command used for the following steps has to support
134	`-F brstack` option. We recommend using `perf` version 4.5 or later.
135	
136	#### For Applications
137	
138	This assumes you can run your program from a command line with a typical input.
139	In this case, simply prepend the command line invocation with `perf`:
140	```
141	$ perf record -e cycles:u -j any,u -o perf.data -- <executable> <args> ...
142	```
143	
144	#### For Services
145	
146	Once you get the service deployed and warmed-up, it is time to collect perf
147	data with brstack (branch information). Different architectures implement this
148	using different hardware units, for example LBR on X86, and BRBE on AArch64.
149	The exact perf command to use will depend on the service. E.g., to collect the
150	data for all processes running on the server for the next 3 minutes use:
151	```
152	$ perf record -e cycles:u -j any,u -a -o perf.data -- sleep 180
153	```
154	
155	Depending on the application, you may need more samples to be included with
156	your profile. It's hard to tell upfront what would be a sweet spot for your
157	application. We recommend the profile to cover 1B instructions as reported
158	by BOLT `-dyno-stats` option. If you need to increase the number of samples
159	in the profile, you can either run the `sleep` command for longer and use
160	`-F<N>` option with `perf` to increase sampling frequency.
161	
162	Note that for profile collection we recommend using cycle events and not
163	`BR_INST_RETIRED.*`. Empirically we found it to produce better results.
164	
165	If the collection of a profile with branches is not available, e.g., when you run on
166	a VM or on hardware that does not support it, then you can use only sample
167	events, such as cycles. In this case, the quality of the profile information
168	would not be as good, and performance gains with BOLT are expected to be lower.
169	
170	#### With instrumentation
171	
172	If perf record is not available to you, you may collect profile by first
173	instrumenting the binary with BOLT and then running it.
174	```
175	llvm-bolt <executable> -instrument -o <instrumented-executable>
176	```
177	
178	After you run instrumented-executable with the desired workload, its BOLT
179	profile should be ready for you in `/tmp/prof.fdata` and you can skip
180	**Step 2**.
181	
182	Run BOLT with the `-help` option and check the category "BOLT instrumentation
183	options" for a quick reference on instrumentation knobs.
184	
185	### Step 2: Convert Profile to BOLT Format
186	
187	NOTE: you can skip this step and feed `perf.data` directly to BOLT using
188	experimental `-p perf.data` option.
189	
190	For this step, you will need `perf.data` file collected from the previous step and
191	a copy of the binary that was running. The binary has to be either
192	unstripped, or should have a symbol table intact (i.e., running `strip -g` is
193	okay).
194	
195	Make sure `perf` is in your `PATH`, and execute `perf2bolt`:
196	```
197	$ perf2bolt -p perf.data -o perf.fdata <executable>
198	```
199	
200	This command will aggregate branch data from `perf.data` and store it in a
201	format that is both more compact and more resilient to binary modifications.
202	
203	If the profile was collected without brstacks, you will need to add `-ba` flag to
204	the command line above.
205	
206	### Step 3: Optimize with BOLT
207	
208	Once you have `perf.fdata` ready, you can use it for optimizations with
209	BOLT. Assuming your environment is setup to include the right path, execute
210	`llvm-bolt`:
211	```
212	$ llvm-bolt <executable> -o <executable>.bolt -data=perf.fdata -reorder-blocks=ext-tsp -reorder-functions=cdsort -split-functions -split-all-cold -split-eh -dyno-stats
213	```
214	
215	If you do need an updated debug info, then add `-update-debug-sections` option
216	to the command above. The processing time will be slightly longer.
217	
218	For a full list of options see `-help`/`-help-hidden` output.
219	
220	The input binary for this step does not have to 100% match the binary used for
221	profile collection in **Step 1**. This could happen when you are doing active
222	development, and the source code constantly changes, yet you want to benefit
223	from profile-guided optimizations. However, since the binary is not precisely the
224	same, the profile information could become invalid or stale, and BOLT will
225	report the number of functions with a stale profile. The higher the
226	number, the less performance improvement should be expected. Thus, it is
227	crucial to update `.fdata` for release branches.
228	
229	## Multiple Profiles
230	
231	Suppose your application can run in different modes, and you can generate
232	multiple profiles for each one of them. To generate a single binary that can
233	benefit all modes (assuming the profiles don't contradict each other) you can
234	use `merge-fdata` tool:
235	```
236	$ merge-fdata *.fdata > combined.fdata
237	```
238	Use `combined.fdata` for **Step 3** above to generate a universally optimized
239	binary.
240	
241	## Identifying a Binary Modified By BOLT
242	
243	A binary that has been modified by BOLT will include a `bolt_info` note and may
244	have extra sections with `bolt` in their name.
245	
246	You can use `readelf` to find these:
247	```
248	$ readelf -S <your-binary> | grep bolt
249	  [11] .bolt.org.eh_frame PROGBITS <...>
250	<...>
251	  [39] .note.bolt_info   NOTE <...>
252	```
253	The note can be displayed with:
254	```
255	$ readelf -p .note.bolt_info <your-binary>
256	String dump of section '.note.bolt_info':
257	  <...>
258	  [    10]  BOLT revision: <...>
259	```
260	
261	## License

263	BOLT is licensed under the [Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions](./LICENSE.TXT).

Depending on the application, you may need more samples to be included with
your profile. It's hard to tell upfront what would be a sweet spot for your
application. We recommend the profile to cover 1B instructions as reported
by BOLT `-dyno-stats` option. If you need to increase the number of samples
in the profile, you can either run the `sleep` command for longer and use
`-F<N>` option with `perf` to increase sampling frequency.

Note that for profile collection we recommend using cycle events and not
`BR_INST_RETIRED.*`. Empirically we found it to produce better results.

If the collection of a profile with branches is not available, e.g., when you run on
a VM or on hardware that does not support it, then you can use only sample
events, such as cycles. In this case, the quality of the profile information
would not be as good, and performance gains with BOLT are expected to be lower.

#### With instrumentation

If perf record is not available to you, you may collect profile by first
instrumenting the binary with BOLT and then running it.
```
llvm-bolt <executable> -instrument -o <instrumented-executable>
```

After you run instrumented-executable with the desired workload, its BOLT
profile should be ready for you in `/tmp/prof.fdata` and you can skip
**Step 2**.

Run BOLT with the `-help` option and check the category "BOLT instrumentation
options" for a quick reference on instrumentation knobs.

### Step 2: Convert Profile to BOLT Format

NOTE: you can skip this step and feed `perf.data` directly to BOLT using
experimental `-p perf.data` option.

For this step, you will need `perf.data` file collected from the previous step and
a copy of the binary that was running. The binary has to be either
unstripped, or should have a symbol table intact (i.e., running `strip -g` is
okay).

Make sure `perf` is in your `PATH`, and execute `perf2bolt`:
```
$ perf2bolt -p perf.data -o perf.fdata <executable>
```

This command will aggregate branch data from `perf.data` and store it in a
format that is both more compact and more resilient to binary modifications.

If the profile was collected without brstacks, you will need to add `-ba` flag to
the command line above.

### Step 3: Optimize with BOLT

Once you have `perf.fdata` ready, you can use it for optimizations with
BOLT. Assuming your environment is setup to include the right path, execute
`llvm-bolt`:
```
$ llvm-bolt <executable> -o <executable>.bolt -data=perf.fdata -reorder-blocks=ext-tsp -reorder-functions=cdsort -split-functions -split-all-cold -split-eh -dyno-stats
```

If you do need an updated debug info, then add `-update-debug-sections` option
to the command above. The processing time will be slightly longer.

For a full list of options see `-help`/`-help-hidden` output.

The input binary for this step does not have to 100% match the binary used for
profile collection in **Step 1**. This could happen when you are doing active
development, and the source code constantly changes, yet you want to benefit
from profile-guided optimizations. However, since the binary is not precisely the
same, the profile information could become invalid or stale, and BOLT will
report the number of functions with a stale profile. The higher the
number, the less performance improvement should be expected. Thus, it is
crucial to update `.fdata` for release branches.

## Multiple Profiles

Suppose your application can run in different modes, and you can generate
multiple profiles for each one of them. To generate a single binary that can
benefit all modes (assuming the profiles don't contradict each other) you can
use `merge-fdata` tool:
```
$ merge-fdata *.fdata > combined.fdata
```
Use `combined.fdata` for **Step 3** above to generate a universally optimized
binary.

## Identifying a Binary Modified By BOLT

A binary that has been modified by BOLT will include a `bolt_info` note and may
have extra sections with `bolt` in their name.

You can use `readelf` to find these:
```
$ readelf -S <your-binary> | grep bolt
  [11] .bolt.org.eh_frame PROGBITS <...>
<...>
  [39] .note.bolt_info   NOTE <...>
```
The note can be displayed with:
```
$ readelf -p .note.bolt_info <your-binary>
String dump of section '.note.bolt_info':
  <...>
  [    10]  BOLT revision: <...>
```

1	# Getting Started with BOLT
2	
3	## Input Binary Requirements
4	
5	BOLT operates on X86-64 and AArch64 ELF binaries. At the minimum, the
6	binaries should have an unstripped symbol table, and, to get maximum
7	performance gains, they should be linked with relocations
8	(`--emit-relocs` or `-q` linker flag).
9	
10	BOLT disassembles functions and reconstructs the control flow graph
11	(CFG) before it runs optimizations. Since this is a nontrivial task,
12	especially when indirect branches are present, we rely on certain
13	heuristics to accomplish it. These heuristics have been tested on a code
14	generated with Clang and GCC compilers. The main requirement for C/C++
15	code is not to rely on code layout properties, such as function pointer
16	deltas. Assembly code can be processed too. Requirements for it include
17	a clear separation of code and data, with data objects being placed into
18	data sections/segments. If indirect jumps are used for intra-function
19	control transfer (e.g., jump tables), the code patterns should be
20	matching those generated by Clang/GCC.
21	
22	NOTE: BOLT is currently incompatible with the
23	`-freorder-blocks-and-partition` compiler option. Since GCC8 enables
24	this option by default, you have to explicitly disable it by adding
25	`-fno-reorder-blocks-and-partition` flag if you are compiling with
26	GCC8 or above.
27	
28	NOTE2: DWARF v5 is the new debugging format generated by the latest LLVM
29	and GCC compilers. It offers several benefits over the previous DWARF
30	v4. Currently, the support for v5 is a work in progress for BOLT. While
31	you will be able to optimize binaries produced by the latest compilers,
32	until the support is complete, you will not be able to update the debug
33	info with `-update-debug-sections`. To temporarily work around the
34	issue, we recommend compiling binaries with `-gdwarf-4` option that
35	forces DWARF v4 output.
36	
37	PIE and .so support has been added recently. Please report bugs if you
38	encounter any issues.
39	
40	## Installation
41	
42	### Docker Image
43	
44	You can build and use the docker image containing BOLT using our [docker
45	file](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/bolt/utils/docker/Dockerfile).
46	Alternatively, you can build BOLT manually using the steps below.
47	
48	### Manual Build
49	
50	BOLT heavily uses LLVM libraries, and by design, it is built as one of

# Getting Started with BOLT

## Input Binary Requirements

BOLT operates on X86-64 and AArch64 ELF binaries. At the minimum, the
binaries should have an unstripped symbol table, and, to get maximum
performance gains, they should be linked with relocations
(`--emit-relocs` or `-q` linker flag).

BOLT disassembles functions and reconstructs the control flow graph
(CFG) before it runs optimizations. Since this is a nontrivial task,
especially when indirect branches are present, we rely on certain
heuristics to accomplish it. These heuristics have been tested on a code
generated with Clang and GCC compilers. The main requirement for C/C++
code is not to rely on code layout properties, such as function pointer
deltas. Assembly code can be processed too. Requirements for it include
a clear separation of code and data, with data objects being placed into
data sections/segments. If indirect jumps are used for intra-function
control transfer (e.g., jump tables), the code patterns should be
matching those generated by Clang/GCC.

NOTE: BOLT is currently incompatible with the
`-freorder-blocks-and-partition` compiler option. Since GCC8 enables
this option by default, you have to explicitly disable it by adding
`-fno-reorder-blocks-and-partition` flag if you are compiling with
GCC8 or above.

NOTE2: DWARF v5 is the new debugging format generated by the latest LLVM
and GCC compilers. It offers several benefits over the previous DWARF
v4. Currently, the support for v5 is a work in progress for BOLT. While
you will be able to optimize binaries produced by the latest compilers,
until the support is complete, you will not be able to update the debug
info with `-update-debug-sections`. To temporarily work around the
issue, we recommend compiling binaries with `-gdwarf-4` option that
forces DWARF v4 output.

PIE and .so support has been added recently. Please report bugs if you
encounter any issues.

## Installation

### Docker Image

You can build and use the docker image containing BOLT using our [docker
file](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/bolt/utils/docker/Dockerfile).
Alternatively, you can build BOLT manually using the steps below.

### Manual Build

BOLT heavily uses LLVM libraries, and by design, it is built as one of
LLVM tools. The build process is not much different from a regular LLVM
build. The following instructions are assuming that you are running
under Linux.

Start with cloning LLVM repo:

```console
> git clone https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project.git
> mkdir build
> cd build
> cmake -G Ninja ../llvm-project/llvm -DLLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="X86;AArch64" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS="bolt"
> ninja bolt
```

`llvm-bolt` will be available under `bin/`. Add this directory to
your path to ensure the rest of the commands in this tutorial work.

## Optimizing BOLT’s Performance

BOLT runs many internal passes in parallel. If you foresee heavy usage
of BOLT, you can improve the processing time by linking against one of
memory allocation libraries with good support for concurrency. E.g. to
use jemalloc:

```console
> sudo yum install jemalloc-devel
> LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libjemalloc.so llvm-bolt ....
```

Or if you rather use tcmalloc:

```console
> sudo yum install gperftools-devel
> LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/libtcmalloc_minimal.so llvm-bolt ....
```

## Usage

For a complete practical guide of using BOLT see {doc}`OptimizingClang`.

### Step 0

In order to allow BOLT to re-arrange functions (in addition to
re-arranging code within functions) in your program, it needs a little
help from the linker. Add `--emit-relocs` to the final link step of
your application. You can verify the presence of relocations by checking
for `.rela.text` section in the binary. BOLT will also report if it
detects relocations while processing the binary.

### Step 1: Collect Profile

This step is different for different kinds of executables. If you can
invoke your program to run on a representative input from a command
line, then check **For Applications** section below. If your program
typically runs as a server/service, then skip to **For Services**
section.

The version of `perf` command used for the following steps has to
support `-F brstack` option. We recommend using `perf` version 4.5
or later.

#### For Applications

This assumes you can run your program from a command line with a typical
input. In this case, simply prepend the command line invocation with
`perf`:

```console
$ perf record -e cycles:u -j any,u -o perf.data -- <executable> <args> ...
```

#### For Services

Once you get the service deployed and warmed-up, it is time to collect
perf data with LBR (branch information). The exact perf command to use
will depend on the service. E.g., to collect the data for all processes
running on the server for the next 3 minutes use:

```console
$ perf record -e cycles:u -j any,u -a -o perf.data -- sleep 180
```

Depending on the application, you may need more samples to be included
with your profile. It’s hard to tell upfront what would be a sweet spot
for your application. We recommend the profile to cover 1B instructions
as reported by BOLT `-dyno-stats` option. If you need to increase the
number of samples in the profile, you can either run the `sleep`
command for longer and use `-F<N>` option with `perf` to increase
sampling frequency.

Note that for profile collection we recommend using cycle events and not
`BR_INST_RETIRED.*`. Empirically we found it to produce better
results.

If the collection of a profile with branches is not available, e.g.,
when you run on a VM or on hardware that does not support it, then you
can use only sample events, such as cycles. In this case, the quality of
the profile information would not be as good, and performance gains with
BOLT are expected to be lower.

#### With instrumentation

If perf record is not available to you, you may collect profile by first
instrumenting the binary with BOLT and then running it.

```console
llvm-bolt <executable> -instrument -o <instrumented-executable>
```

After you run instrumented-executable with the desired workload, its
BOLT profile should be ready for you in `/tmp/prof.fdata` and you can
skip **Step 2**.

Run BOLT with the `-help` option and check the category “BOLT
instrumentation options” for a quick reference on instrumentation knobs.

### Step 2: Convert Profile to BOLT Format

NOTE: you can skip this step and feed `perf.data` directly to BOLT
using experimental `-p perf.data` option.

For this step, you will need `perf.data` file collected from the
previous step and a copy of the binary that was running. The binary has
to be either unstripped, or should have a symbol table intact (i.e.,
running `strip -g` is okay).

Make sure `perf` is in your `PATH`, and execute `perf2bolt`:

```console
$ perf2bolt -p perf.data -o perf.fdata <executable>
```

This command will aggregate branch data from `perf.data` and store it
in a format that is both more compact and more resilient to binary
modifications.

If the profile was collected without brstacks, you will need to add `-ba` flag to
the command line above.

### Step 3: Optimize with BOLT

Once you have `perf.fdata` ready, you can use it for optimizations
with BOLT. Assuming your environment is setup to include the right path,
execute `llvm-bolt`:

```console
$ llvm-bolt <executable> -o <executable>.bolt -data=perf.fdata -reorder-blocks=ext-tsp -reorder-functions=hfsort -split-functions -split-all-cold -split-eh -dyno-stats
```

If you do need an updated debug info, then add
`-update-debug-sections` option to the command above. The processing
time will be slightly longer.

For a full list of options see `-help`/`-help-hidden` output.

The input binary for this step does not have to 100% match the binary
used for profile collection in **Step 1**. This could happen when you
are doing active development, and the source code constantly changes,
yet you want to benefit from profile-guided optimizations. However,
since the binary is not precisely the same, the profile information
could become invalid or stale, and BOLT will report the number of
functions with a stale profile. The higher the number, the less
performance improvement should be expected. Thus, it is crucial to
update `.fdata` for release branches.

## Multiple Profiles

Suppose your application can run in different modes, and you can
generate multiple profiles for each one of them. To generate a single
binary that can benefit all modes (assuming the profiles don’t
contradict each other) you can use `merge-fdata` tool:

```console
$ merge-fdata *.fdata > combined.fdata
```

Use `combined.fdata` for **Step 3** above to generate a universally
optimized binary.

## Profile Formats

See {doc}`profiles` for comprehensive documentation of all profile formats
accepted by BOLT: perf.data, fdata, YAML, and pre-aggregated.

## License

BOLT is licensed under the [Apache License v2.0 with LLVM
Exceptions](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/LICENSE.TXT).

learning_goals: 掌握 bolt/ 下 lib/Core、lib/Passes、lib/Profile、lib/Rewrite、lib/Target 各自职责
理解 main() 按 argv[0] 名字分发的多模式机制
理清 ELF 走 RewriteInstance、Mach-O 走 MachORewriteInstance 的入口分流
minimal_modules: 目标初始化宏 BOLT_TARGET 与 createBinary 后的分流
lectures.practice_task: 在 tools/driver/llvm-bolt.cpp 中找到根据 argv[0] 判断 perf2bolt/boltdiff/bolt 模式的代码，画出 main() 从打开二进制到调用 RewriteInstance::run()/MachORewriteInstance::run() 的调用流程图。

units.title: 核心数据结构：BinaryContext、BinaryFunction 与 MCPlus

lectures.title: BinaryContext：贯穿全局的中心上下文
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryContext 作为全局中枢的角色：它持有所有 BinaryFunction 的映射、MCPlusBuilder、DWARFContext、各 section/symbol/relocation 索引，以及日志流与目标信息。
learning_goals: 理解 BinaryContext 持有哪些全局状态（BinaryFunctions、符号表、DWARFContext）
掌握 MCPlusBuilder、目标架构判断（isX86/isAArch64/isRISCV）的作用
理解 createBinaryFunction 与 getBinaryFunctionAtAddress 等查找接口
minimal_modules: BinaryContext 的核心成员与职责
函数映射与符号到函数的索引
目标/调试信息/日志流接入
lectures.practice_task: 在 BinaryContext.h 中找出 BinaryFunctions 容器的类型与 getBinaryFunctions() 访问器，并定位 initializeTarget 如何接收 MCPlusBuilder；写一小段伪代码说明如何通过 BC 遍历所有函数并按地址查找函数。

lectures.title: BinaryFunction 与状态机：一个函数在 BOLT 中的生命周期
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryFunction 如何表示一个被处理的函数：指令表（InstrMapType）、基本块、FunctionLayout、CFI 状态，以及 Empty→Disassembled→CFG 的状态机。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryFunction::State 状态机（Empty/Disassembled/CFG 等）
理解指令表（offset→MCInst）与 FunctionLayout 的关系
理解 isSimple 标志对函数能否被优化的影响
minimal_modules: Simple/非 Simple 函数的区分
lectures.practice_task: 在 BinaryFunction.h 中找到 enum class State 的定义并列出各状态；阅读 clearDisasmState()/resetState()，说明当函数反汇编失败时如何回退状态，并解释为什么非 simple 函数不能被常规优化。

lectures.title: BinaryBasicBlock 与控制流图表示
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryBasicBlock 如何作为 CFG 节点：它持有指令范围、后继/前驱边、分支类型、执行计数，以及 BinaryDomTree/BinaryLoop 提供的支配与循环信息。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryBasicBlock 的指令管理与后继/前驱边维护
理解分支类型（条件/无条件/直接/间接）的表示
了解 BinaryDomTree 与 BinaryLoop 提供的分析结构
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 BinaryBasicBlock 的 addSuccessor/removeSuccessor 相关接口，写一段说明 CFG 边是如何维护双向一致性的；并用 BinaryDomTree/BinaryLoop 说明如何在 BOLT 里获取一个块的支配者与所属循环。

lectures.title: MCPlus：在 MCInst 之上挂载元数据的扩展机制
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 的核心创新之一 MCPlus：通过在 MCInst 末尾追加额外 operand 来承载注释（annotation），分为影响语义的一等注释（EH/跳转表）和可丢弃的补充注释（profile/debug）。
learning_goals: 理解 MCPlus 如何用 extra operand 把元数据挂到 MCInst 上
区分一等注释（影响正确性）与补充注释（可丢弃）
理解 MCPlusBuilder 作为目标无关接口创建/解析注释的角色
minimal_modules: MCPlus 注释的存储原理（kInst operand 标记起点）
一等注释 vs 补充注释
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 include/bolt/Core/MCPlus.h 顶部的注释，说明 MCPlus 用哪个 operand 类型标记注释的开始；列出两类注释的例子，并解释为什么把 profile 计数做成补充注释是安全的。

units.title: 主处理链路：跟着 RewriteInstance::run() 走

lectures.title: RewriteInstance::run() 全流程总览
lectures.topic: 通读 RewriteInstance::run() 的完整阶段序列，建立对 BOLT 主链路（发现→反汇编→CFG→profile→优化→发射→重写文件）的整体认知。
learning_goals: 掌握 run() 的完整阶段顺序与每个阶段的职责
理解 DiffOnly/BinaryAnalysisMode/Instrument 等模式如何分流
建立从输入二进制到输出二进制的全链路心智模型
minimal_modules: 各阶段对应的 NamedRegionTimer 计时
lectures.practice_task: 对照 RewriteInstance.cpp 中 run() 的实现，按执行顺序列出所有阶段函数名；标注哪些阶段在 DiffOnly 时被跳过，并说明 -time-rewrite 如何通过 NamedRegionTimer 记录每个阶段耗时。

lectures.title: 二进制发现与特殊 section 解析
lectures.topic: 讲清 discoverStorage、readSpecialSections、discoverFileObjects 如何从 ELF 中识别函数符号、建立 BinarySection 与 BinaryData、并解析 .eh_frame 等特殊 section。
learning_goals: 掌握函数如何从符号表被发现为 BinaryFunction
理解 BinarySection 的抽象与 section 内容管理
了解 eh_frame/plt/rela 等特殊 section 的早期解析
lectures.practice_task: 在 RewriteInstance.cpp 中找到 discoverFileObjects()，说明它如何利用 FILE 符号区分同名局部函数；并列出 readSpecialSections() 至少解析的 3 类特殊 section 及其用途。

lectures.title: 反汇编与 CFG 重建：processIndirectBranch 与启发式
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryFunction::disassemble() 与 buildCFG() 如何把字节流变成 CFG，重点在间接分支（跳转表/间接跳转）的 processIndirectBranch 启发式判定。
learning_goals: 掌握 disassemble() 如何逐指令解码并建立指令表
理解 buildCFG() 如何切分基本块、连接边
理解 processIndirectBranch 如何判定跳转表与间接跳转类型
minimal_modules: 指令解码与指令表构建
基本块切分与 CFG 构建
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 BinaryFunction::disassemble() 与 buildCFG()，画出从原始字节到 CFG 的转换步骤；列出 processIndirectBranch 返回的 IndirectBranchType 枚举值，并说明为什么间接跳转的识别依赖启发式而非确定算法。

lectures.title: 重定位与 JumpTable：--emit-relocs 的意义
lectures.topic: 讲清 Relocation 抽象与 .rela.text 的作用：emit-relocs 让 BOLT 能安全移动代码与数据；同时讲 JumpTable 如何作为数据/代码混合实体被识别和重写。
learning_goals: 理解为什么需要 --emit-relocs 才能移动函数
掌握 Relocation 抽象及其在代码/数据移动时的修正
理解 JumpTable（代码内的数据）如何被识别与处理
lectures.practice_task: 在 README/GettingStarted 中找到关于 --emit-relocs 与 .rela.text 的说明，并在 Relocation.cpp 中定位重定位信息如何被读取与修正；解释如果没有 relocations，BOLT 为什么不能重排函数。

units.title: Profile 子系统：perf、fdata、YAML 与 BAT

lectures.title: Profile 格式总览与 fdata/DataReader
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 接受的多种 profile 格式（perf.data、fdata、YAML、BAT）与统一的 ProfileReaderBase 抽象，并深入 fdata 文本格式与 DataReader 的解析。
learning_goals: 掌握 BOLT 支持的 profile 格式及其选择逻辑
理解 setProfile 如何按文件魔数/YAML 选择 reader
读懂 fdata 文本格式与 DataReader 解析流程
minimal_modules: fdata 格式与 DataReader 解析
lectures.practice_task: 在 RewriteInstance::setProfile 中画出按文件类型选择 DataAggregator/YAMLProfileReader/DataReader 的判定逻辑；手写一个最小 fdata 样例文件并说明每字段的含义。

lectures.title: perf2bolt 与 DataAggregator：从 perf.data 聚合分支数据
lectures.topic: 讲清 perf2bolt 模式如何用 DataAggregator 解析 perf.data（brstack/LBR），聚合分支计数，并输出更紧凑稳定的 fdata。
learning_goals: 理解 perf2bolt 模式（AggregateOnly）与 brstack/LBR 的关系
掌握 DataAggregator 解析 perf.data 的流程
理解聚合后 fdata 为何更稳定（地址无关）
minimal_modules: 分支数据聚合与 fdata 输出
lectures.practice_task: 对照 tools/driver/llvm-bolt.cpp 的 perf2boltMode()，说明 AggregateOnly/ShowDensity 如何被设置；在 DataAggregator 中找到 checkPerfDataMagic，解释为什么可以直接把 perf.data 喂给 llvm-bolt（-p）而跳过 perf2bolt。

lectures.title: Bolt Address Translation（BAT）：从优化后二进制回采 profile
lectures.topic: 讲清 BAT 机制：BOLT 在输出二进制中插入 .note.bolt_bat，记录地址翻译表，使后续能从 BOLT 优化过的二进制采集 profile 并映射回原始输入二进制再次优化。
learning_goals: 理解 BAT 解决的痛点（迭代优化的 profile 采集）
掌握 .note.bolt_bat section 的结构与用途
理解 --enable-bat 与 perf2bolt 的配合
minimal_modules: BAT section 结构（热/冷函数表）
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 docs/BAT.md，用一段话解释为什么没有 BAT 就很难对已优化的二进制再次迭代优化；用 bat-dump 工具的源码（tools/bat-dump/bat-dump.cpp）说明如何读取并展示 BAT section。

lectures.title: Heatmap 可视化与 Stale Profile Matching
lectures.topic: 讲清两个 profile 相关能力：Heatmap 工具/类把 profile 密度可视化为热点地图；StaleProfileMatching 在二进制与采集时已不一致（stale）时尽量匹配 profile。
learning_goals: 理解 Heatmap 如何表达代码热点分布
掌握 stale profile 的成因与 StaleProfileMatching 的匹配思路
会用 heatmap 工具与 -dyno-stats 评估 profile 质量
lectures.practice_task: 用 heatmap 工具（参照 docs/Heatmaps.md）对一个带 profile 的二进制生成热点图，并解释横纵坐标的含义；阅读 StaleProfileMatching.cpp 的入口，说明它在什么情况下被触发、用什么策略匹配旧 profile。

units.title: Pass 框架：注册、顺序、并行与统计

lectures.title: BinaryFunctionPassManager：pass 框架、顺序与并行
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 的 pass 基础设施：BinaryFunctionPass 基类、registerPass/runAllPasses 的注册与顺序、runOnFunctions 的并行执行（ParallelUtilities）、DynoStats 与 VerifyCFG。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryFunctionPass 基类与 runOnFunctions 接口
理解 runAllPasses 中 pass 的注册顺序即执行顺序
理解 ParallelUtilities 如何并行、DynoStats/VerifyCFG 如何校验
lectures.practice_task: 在 BinaryPassManager.cpp 的 runPasses() 中，说明 pass 是否执行取决于注册时的哪个布尔参数；并解释 ParallelUtilities::runOnEachFunctionWithUniqueAllocId 在 disassembleFunctions 中如何避免多线程 MCPlus allocator 冲突。

lectures.title: 基础整理 pass：从 NormalizeCFG 到 FinalizeFunctions
lectures.topic: 挑出贯穿管线的基础 pass 讲清它们的作用：NormalizeCFG、ShortenInstructions、RemoveNops、FixupBranches、AssignSections、FinalizeFunctions、InstructionLowering 等。
learning_goals: 理解 NormalizeCFG 如何规整 CFG 以便后续优化
掌握 FixupBranches 与 FinalizeFunctions 为何要在布局确定后运行
理解 InstructionLowering 把伪指令落地为真实指令的时机
lectures.practice_task: 在 runAllPasses() 中找出注释里强调'必须最后运行'或'依赖最终布局'的 pass（如 FinalizeFunctions、FixupBranches、CleanMCState），各写一句话说明它们为什么必须在那个位置。

lectures.title: Identical Code Folding（ICF）：折叠相同函数体
lectures.topic: 讲清 ICF 如何检测字节级/语义级相同的函数并折叠为一个，以减少代码体积；并说明它在管线中运行两次的原因。
learning_goals: 理解 ICF 检测相同函数的原理与安全条件
掌握 ICF level 选项与正确性约束
理解为何 ICF 在 Inliner 前后各运行一次
minimal_modules: ICF level 与安全性（hash/语义）
管线中两次 ICF 的位置
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 IdenticalCodeFolding.cpp 的入口，说明它用什么粒度（指令序列/重定位/符号）判定两个函数相同；并在 runAllPasses() 中找出 ICF 的两次注册位置，解释为什么 Inliner 之后需要再跑一次。

units.title: 核心优化 pass：布局、分裂与调用优化

lectures.title: 基本块排序与 Ext-TSP 布局算法
lectures.topic: 讲清 ReorderBasicBlocks pass 与背后的 ReorderAlgorithm 体系，重点 Ext-TSP（扩展旅行商）算法如何用 profile 在基本块/簇级别最小化分支与缓存代价。
learning_goals: 掌握 ClusterAlgorithm 与 ReorderAlgorithm 的类层次
理解 Ext-TSP 评分模型（fall-through、跳转距离、缓存密度）
理解 -reorder-blocks 各取值如何选择算法
lectures.practice_task: 在 ReorderAlgorithm.h 中列出 ReorderAlgorithm 的所有子类与对应 Cluster 算法；阅读 ExtTSPReorderAlgorithm，用一段话解释它的评分函数如何同时考虑 fall-through 命中率与跳转距离，并说明 ext-tsp 为何是默认选项。

lectures.title: 函数排序：HFSort、Pettis-Hansen、CDSort 与 MCF
lectures.topic: 讲清 ReorderFunctions pass 与函数级布局算法（HFSort、Pettis-Hansen、CDSort），以及 CallGraph/CallGraphWalker 与 MCF（最小割流）在调用图聚簇中的作用。
learning_goals: 理解函数级布局为何要用调用图聚簇
掌握 HFSort/Pettis-Hansen/CDSort 的差异与 -reorder-functions 选项
理解 CallGraph、CallGraphWalker 与 MCF 的角色
lectures.practice_task: 对比 HFSort.cpp、PettisAndHansen.cpp 与 MCF.cpp 三种聚簇/排序策略的核心思想（各一句）；阅读 ReorderFunctions.cpp，说明它如何根据 -reorder-functions 选择算法，以及 PopulateOutputFunctions 如何把排序结果落地为输出顺序。

lectures.title: SplitFunctions：热冷分裂与 cdsplit
lectures.topic: 讲清 SplitFunctions 如何把函数的冷基本块拆到独立 .text.cold section，以及为何在 ReorderFunctions 之后会第二次运行（支持 hot-warm-cold 的 cdsplit 策略）。
learning_goals: 掌握热冷分裂的收益（提升指令缓存局部性）
理解 FunctionFragment 与分裂的判定阈值
理解管线中两次 SplitFunctions 的不同目的
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 SplitFunctions.cpp 的核心逻辑，说明如何根据执行计数判定一个基本块是否冷；在 runAllPasses() 中找到两次 SplitFunctions 注册，解释为什么第二次要在 ReorderFunctions 之后（参考源码注释）。

lectures.title: 调用相关优化：ICP、Inliner、SCTC 与 PLT
lectures.topic: 讲清几个直接改造调用图的 pass：IndirectCallPromotion（ICP，热点间接调用转直接）、Inliner、SimplifyConditionalTailCalls（SCTC，条件尾调用转跳转）、PLTCall。
learning_goals: 理解 ICP 如何用 profile 把热点间接调用转成直接调用梯子
掌握 BOLT 二进制级 inlining 的特点与限制
理解 SCTC 如何消除条件尾调用的冗余跳转
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 IndirectCallPromotion.cpp，说明它如何根据 profile 选择被提升的间接调用目标并构建比较-直接调用梯子；并解释 SCTC 为什么必须放在 ReorderFunctions 之后运行（参考 runAllPasses 注释）。

lectures.title: 栈帧与寄存器优化：FrameOptimizer、RegReAssign、ShrinkWrapping
lectures.topic: 讲清依赖数据流分析的进阶 pass：FrameOptimizer（利用栈帧分析省去存取）、RegReAssign（重分配寄存器）、ShrinkWrapping（收缩 prologue/epilogue 范围），以及它们依赖的 FrameAnalysis/LivenessAnalysis。
learning_goals: 理解 FrameOptimizer 依赖的栈帧数据流分析
掌握 RegReAssign 如何用 profile 重新分配寄存器
理解 ShrinkWrapping 收缩 prologue/epilogue 的收益与风险
lectures.practice_task: 在 runAllPasses() 中找到 FrameOptimizerPass 并阅读注释，解释它为何必须依赖 FinalizeFunctions（需要正确放置 CFI）；列出它读取/改写 CFI 所需的栈帧分析来自哪个 pass。

units.title: 目标后端与代码生成：MCPlusBuilder、发射与链接

lectures.title: MCPlusBuilder 后端抽象与新增后端
lectures.topic: 讲清 MCPlusBuilder/MCSymbolizer 作为目标无关接口的职责，X86/AArch64/RISCV 三个实现如何差异；并依据 NewBackend.md 讲清如何新增一个 BOLT 后端。
learning_goals: 掌握 MCPlusBuilder 抽象了哪些目标相关能力（建指令/分析/分支范围）
理解 X86/AArch64/RISCV 三个实现的差异（如 LongJmp 放松）
理解新增后端的步骤与必须先落地的公共改动
lectures.practice_task: 对照 docs/NewBackend.md，列出新增后端至少要在哪些目录实现什么（MCPlusBuilder、Relocation.cpp 的平台处理、测试）；并说明 RISCV 为何需要 LongJmp/branch relaxation 而 X86 通常不需要。

lectures.title: BinaryEmitter 与 JITLinkLinker：发射函数与 ORC 链接
lectures.topic: 讲清 emitAndLink 阶段：BinaryEmitter 用 MCStreamer 把优化后的函数重新发射为可链接对象，JITLinkLinker 基于 LLVM ORC 把它链接回内存以得到最终地址。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryEmitter 如何遍历 FunctionLayout 发射每个 fragment
理解 emitFunctionBody 如何处理指令、CFI、行号信息
理解 JITLinkLinker 基于 ORC 的 loadObject/lookupSymbolInfo 机制
minimal_modules: emitAndLink 在 run() 中的位置
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 BinaryEmitter::emitAll/emitFunctions，说明它如何按 FunctionLayout 发射主 fragment 与冷 fragment；对照 docs/RuntimeLibrary.md 解释 JITLinkLinker 这个'极简链接器'为什么只能做基本的符号解析（与 freestanding 运行库的限制呼应）。

units.title: 二进制重写细节：调试信息、运行时库与元数据

lectures.title: DWARF/调试信息重写：DWARFRewriter 与 DIEBuilder
lectures.topic: 讲清 -update-debug-sections 如何在 BOLT 移动代码后修正 DWARF 调试信息：DWARFRewriter、DIEBuilder、DebugData、GDBIndex、AddressMap 如何协同重建 .debug_* 与地址映射。
learning_goals: 理解移动代码后为何必须重写 DWARF 才能保留可调试性
掌握 DIEBuilder 如何重建 DIE 树与地址范围
理解 AddressMap/.gdb_index 等辅助映射的作用
minimal_modules: DWARF 重写的必要性与 DWARF v4/v5 现状
lectures.practice_task: 在 GettingStarted.md 中找到关于 -update-debug-sections 与 -gdwarf-4 的说明，解释 DWARF v5 支持的现状；阅读 DWARFRewriter 的入口，列出它需要修正的至少 3 类调试 section（如 .debug_info/.debug_line/.debug_ranges）。

lectures.title: 运行时库与插桩：RuntimeLibrary、Instrumentation 与 Hugify
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 注入辅助代码的机制：RuntimeLibrary 基类、InstrumentationRuntimeLibrary（-instrument 插桩采集）与 HugifyRuntimeLibrary（大页），以及 runtime/ 下 freestanding 的 C++ 运行库代码。
learning_goals: 理解运行时库注入的层级（MCPlusBuilder 小改 vs 运行库大改）
掌握 Instrumentation 如何生成计数并写 /tmp/prof.fdata
理解 runtime/ 为何要 freestanding（-ffreestanding，无 BSS/无依赖）
lectures.practice_task: 对照 docs/RuntimeLibrary.md，列出 runtime/ 运行库必须遵守的 freestanding 约束（如无 BSS、无外部依赖、只用裸 .text/.data）；阅读 Instrumentation.cpp，说明 -instrument 模式如何在函数内插入计数代码并最终写出 prof.fdata。

lectures.title: 元数据与特殊 section 重写：MetadataManager 与各类 Rewriter
lectures.topic: 讲清 finalizeMetadataPreEmit/updateMetadata/rewriteFile 阶段如何处理非函数的元数据 section：MetadataManager 统一调度 LinuxKernel/RSeq/PseudoProbe/SDT/GNUProperty/BuildID/eh_frame 等重写器。
learning_goals: 掌握 MetadataManager 如何统一管理元数据重写器的生命周期
理解 .eh_frame/eh_frame_hdr 异常处理表的重写
了解 Linux kernel / RSeq / PseudoProbe / SDT 等特殊场景的重写
minimal_modules: Linux kernel / RSeq 特殊重写
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 include/bolt/Rewrite/MetadataRewriters.h，列出所有元数据重写器类；在 run() 中定位 processMetadataPreCFG/processMetadataPostCFG/finalizeMetadataPreEmit/updateMetadata，说明元数据重写为何分散在多个阶段而非一次完成。

units.title: 工程实践：测试体系与辅助工具

data.head: abe5aa5cb2336f32dca8e765710ec212a926476c
data.rationale: 本大纲按「先认识、再读数据结构、再走主链路、再深入子系统和优化、最后到代码生成/重写/工程实践」的顺序，把 BOLT 这个二进制后链接优化器拆成 9 个单元 31 篇讲义。单元 1 让读者从零认识项目并跑通端到端流程；单元 2 讲清贯穿全工程的四大核心数据结构（BinaryContext、BinaryFunction、BasicBlock/CFG、MCPlus 元数据），它们是后续所有源码阅读的基础；单元 3 顺着 RewriteInstance::run() 的真实调用链讲主处理流程（发现→反汇编→CFG→重定位）；单元 4 专门讲 Profile 子系统，因为 BOLT 是 profile-guided 的，profile 质量直接决定效果；单元 5 建立 pass 框架的心智模型（注册、顺序、并行、DynoStats、VerifyCFG），这是理解单元 6 各优化 pass 的前提；单元 6 是 BOLT 的核心价值所在——block/function 排序、热冷分裂、调用优化、栈帧与寄存器优化；单元 7 讲目标后端抽象与代码生成（发射+ORC 链接）；单元 8 讲二进制重写最难的调试信息重写、运行时库/插桩和元数据/特殊 section 重写；单元 9 收尾于测试体系与辅助工具/性能调优。讲义之间依赖关系严格遵循「先框架后细节、先公共后特化」的原则，每篇只解决一个主题并配一个可操作的源码实践任务。

units.title: 认识 BOLT：项目定位、构建运行与端到端流程

lectures.title: BOLT 是什么：后链接二进制优化器的定位与原理
lectures.topic: 讲清楚 BOLT 作为 post-link（链接后）profile-guided 二进制优化器的定位：它接收已链接的 ELF 二进制，反汇编重建 CFG，再基于 perf 采样 profile 重新布局代码以提升指令缓存与分支预测表现。
learning_goals: 理解后链接优化与编译期 PGO 的区别与互补关系
掌握 BOLT 的输入要求（未 strip、--emit-relocs、X86-64/AArch64 ELF）
理解 BOLT 优化的核心收益来源（代码布局、热冷分离）
minimal_modules: BOLT 的定位与历史（CGO'19 论文背景）
输入二进制要求与限制
BOLT 优化能带来什么收益
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 README.md，用一句话写出 BOLT 与编译器 -O3 优化的本质区别；并列出对输入二进制必须满足的 3 个条件，说明每个条件为什么必要。

lectures.title: 构建与运行 BOLT：CMake 构建、目标架构与工具一览
lectures.topic: 讲清楚如何把 BOLT 作为 LLVM 子项目构建出来，理解 CMake 选项与目标架构选择，并认识 bin/ 下产生的各个工具。
learning_goals: 掌握 -DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=bolt 的构建流程
理解 LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD 与 BOLT 支持架构的关系
认识 llvm-bolt、perf2bolt、merge-fdata、heatmap、bat-dump 等可执行文件
minimal_modules: 顶层 CMakeLists.txt 如何挂载为 LLVM 子项目
构建命令与 ninja bolt 目标
bin/ 下各工具的用途速览
lectures.practice_task: 按照 GettingStarted.md 写出完整的 cmake + ninja 构建命令（含 X86;AArch64 两个目标）；在 CMakeLists.txt 中找到设置 LLVM_SUBPROJECT_TITLE 为 BOLT 的行，说明它如何让 BOLT 成为 LLVM 树的一部分。

lectures.title: 端到端使用流程：从 perf 采集到 BOLT 优化
lectures.topic: 通过 OptimizingClang 实操文档讲清 BOLT 的四步标准流程：Step0 emit-relocs 链接、Step1 perf 采集、Step2 perf2bolt 转 fdata、Step3 llvm-bolt 优化。
learning_goals: 掌握 perf record 采集分支采样（-j any,u / brstack）的方法
理解 perf2bolt 把 perf.data 聚合为 fdata 的作用
会用 -reorder-blocks/-reorder-functions/-split-functions 等关键选项运行优化
minimal_modules: 插桩（-instrument）作为替代采集方式
lectures.practice_task: 以一个简单的 hello world 程序为例（或参照 OptimizingClang），写出从 -Wl,-q 链接、perf record 采集、perf2bolt 转换到 llvm-bolt -reorder-blocks=ext-tsp -split-functions -dyno-stats 优化的完整命令序列，并用 -dyno-stats 对比优化前后的指令统计。

lectures.title: 代码目录结构与程序入口
lectures.topic: 讲清 bolt/ 顶层目录划分（lib/include/tools/test/runtime/docs）以及主入口 tools/driver/llvm-bolt.cpp 中 main() 如何根据 argv[0] 分发到 bolt/perf2bolt/boltdiff 三种模式。
learning_goals: 掌握 bolt/ 下 lib/Core、lib/Passes、lib/Profile、lib/Rewrite、lib/Target 各自职责
理解 main() 按 argv[0] 名字分发的多模式机制
理清 ELF 走 RewriteInstance、Mach-O 走 MachORewriteInstance 的入口分流
minimal_modules: 目标初始化宏 BOLT_TARGET 与 createBinary 后的分流
lectures.practice_task: 在 tools/driver/llvm-bolt.cpp 中找到根据 argv[0] 判断 perf2bolt/boltdiff/bolt 模式的代码，画出 main() 从打开二进制到调用 RewriteInstance::run()/MachORewriteInstance::run() 的调用流程图。

units.title: 核心数据结构：BinaryContext、BinaryFunction 与 MCPlus

lectures.title: BinaryContext：贯穿全局的中心上下文
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryContext 作为全局中枢的角色：它持有所有 BinaryFunction 的映射、MCPlusBuilder、DWARFContext、各 section/symbol/relocation 索引，以及日志流与目标信息。
learning_goals: 理解 BinaryContext 持有哪些全局状态（BinaryFunctions、符号表、DWARFContext）
掌握 MCPlusBuilder、目标架构判断（isX86/isAArch64/isRISCV）的作用
理解 createBinaryFunction 与 getBinaryFunctionAtAddress 等查找接口
minimal_modules: BinaryContext 的核心成员与职责
函数映射与符号到函数的索引
目标/调试信息/日志流接入
lectures.practice_task: 在 BinaryContext.h 中找出 BinaryFunctions 容器的类型与 getBinaryFunctions() 访问器，并定位 initializeTarget 如何接收 MCPlusBuilder；写一小段伪代码说明如何通过 BC 遍历所有函数并按地址查找函数。

lectures.title: BinaryFunction 与状态机：一个函数在 BOLT 中的生命周期
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryFunction 如何表示一个被处理的函数：指令表（InstrMapType）、基本块、FunctionLayout、CFI 状态，以及 Empty→Disassembled→CFG 的状态机。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryFunction::State 状态机（Empty/Disassembled/CFG 等）
理解指令表（offset→MCInst）与 FunctionLayout 的关系
理解 isSimple 标志对函数能否被优化的影响
minimal_modules: Simple/非 Simple 函数的区分
lectures.practice_task: 在 BinaryFunction.h 中找到 enum class State 的定义并列出各状态；阅读 clearDisasmState()/resetState()，说明当函数反汇编失败时如何回退状态，并解释为什么非 simple 函数不能被常规优化。

lectures.title: BinaryBasicBlock 与控制流图表示
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryBasicBlock 如何作为 CFG 节点：它持有指令范围、后继/前驱边、分支类型、执行计数，以及 BinaryDomTree/BinaryLoop 提供的支配与循环信息。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryBasicBlock 的指令管理与后继/前驱边维护
理解分支类型（条件/无条件/直接/间接）的表示
了解 BinaryDomTree 与 BinaryLoop 提供的分析结构
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 BinaryBasicBlock 的 addSuccessor/removeSuccessor 相关接口，写一段说明 CFG 边是如何维护双向一致性的；并用 BinaryDomTree/BinaryLoop 说明如何在 BOLT 里获取一个块的支配者与所属循环。

lectures.title: MCPlus：在 MCInst 之上挂载元数据的扩展机制
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 的核心创新之一 MCPlus：通过在 MCInst 末尾追加额外 operand 来承载注释（annotation），分为影响语义的一等注释（EH/跳转表）和可丢弃的补充注释（profile/debug）。
learning_goals: 理解 MCPlus 如何用 extra operand 把元数据挂到 MCInst 上
区分一等注释（影响正确性）与补充注释（可丢弃）
理解 MCPlusBuilder 作为目标无关接口创建/解析注释的角色
minimal_modules: MCPlus 注释的存储原理（kInst operand 标记起点）
一等注释 vs 补充注释
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 include/bolt/Core/MCPlus.h 顶部的注释，说明 MCPlus 用哪个 operand 类型标记注释的开始；列出两类注释的例子，并解释为什么把 profile 计数做成补充注释是安全的。

units.title: 主处理链路：跟着 RewriteInstance::run() 走

lectures.title: RewriteInstance::run() 全流程总览
lectures.topic: 通读 RewriteInstance::run() 的完整阶段序列，建立对 BOLT 主链路（发现→反汇编→CFG→profile→优化→发射→重写文件）的整体认知。
learning_goals: 掌握 run() 的完整阶段顺序与每个阶段的职责
理解 DiffOnly/BinaryAnalysisMode/Instrument 等模式如何分流
建立从输入二进制到输出二进制的全链路心智模型
minimal_modules: 各阶段对应的 NamedRegionTimer 计时
lectures.practice_task: 对照 RewriteInstance.cpp 中 run() 的实现，按执行顺序列出所有阶段函数名；标注哪些阶段在 DiffOnly 时被跳过，并说明 -time-rewrite 如何通过 NamedRegionTimer 记录每个阶段耗时。

lectures.title: 二进制发现与特殊 section 解析
lectures.topic: 讲清 discoverStorage、readSpecialSections、discoverFileObjects 如何从 ELF 中识别函数符号、建立 BinarySection 与 BinaryData、并解析 .eh_frame 等特殊 section。
learning_goals: 掌握函数如何从符号表被发现为 BinaryFunction
理解 BinarySection 的抽象与 section 内容管理
了解 eh_frame/plt/rela 等特殊 section 的早期解析
lectures.practice_task: 在 RewriteInstance.cpp 中找到 discoverFileObjects()，说明它如何利用 FILE 符号区分同名局部函数；并列出 readSpecialSections() 至少解析的 3 类特殊 section 及其用途。

lectures.title: 反汇编与 CFG 重建：processIndirectBranch 与启发式
lectures.topic: 讲清 BinaryFunction::disassemble() 与 buildCFG() 如何把字节流变成 CFG，重点在间接分支（跳转表/间接跳转）的 processIndirectBranch 启发式判定。
learning_goals: 掌握 disassemble() 如何逐指令解码并建立指令表
理解 buildCFG() 如何切分基本块、连接边
理解 processIndirectBranch 如何判定跳转表与间接跳转类型
minimal_modules: 指令解码与指令表构建
基本块切分与 CFG 构建
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 BinaryFunction::disassemble() 与 buildCFG()，画出从原始字节到 CFG 的转换步骤；列出 processIndirectBranch 返回的 IndirectBranchType 枚举值，并说明为什么间接跳转的识别依赖启发式而非确定算法。

lectures.title: 重定位与 JumpTable：--emit-relocs 的意义
lectures.topic: 讲清 Relocation 抽象与 .rela.text 的作用：emit-relocs 让 BOLT 能安全移动代码与数据；同时讲 JumpTable 如何作为数据/代码混合实体被识别和重写。
learning_goals: 理解为什么需要 --emit-relocs 才能移动函数
掌握 Relocation 抽象及其在代码/数据移动时的修正
理解 JumpTable（代码内的数据）如何被识别与处理
lectures.practice_task: 在 README/GettingStarted 中找到关于 --emit-relocs 与 .rela.text 的说明，并在 Relocation.cpp 中定位重定位信息如何被读取与修正；解释如果没有 relocations，BOLT 为什么不能重排函数。

units.title: Profile 子系统：perf、fdata、YAML 与 BAT

lectures.title: Profile 格式总览与 fdata/DataReader
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 接受的多种 profile 格式（perf.data、fdata、YAML、BAT）与统一的 ProfileReaderBase 抽象，并深入 fdata 文本格式与 DataReader 的解析。
learning_goals: 掌握 BOLT 支持的 profile 格式及其选择逻辑
理解 setProfile 如何按文件魔数/YAML 选择 reader
读懂 fdata 文本格式与 DataReader 解析流程
minimal_modules: fdata 格式与 DataReader 解析
lectures.practice_task: 在 RewriteInstance::setProfile 中画出按文件类型选择 DataAggregator/YAMLProfileReader/DataReader 的判定逻辑；手写一个最小 fdata 样例文件并说明每字段的含义。

lectures.title: perf2bolt 与 DataAggregator：从 perf.data 聚合分支数据
lectures.topic: 讲清 perf2bolt 模式如何用 DataAggregator 解析 perf.data（brstack/LBR），聚合分支计数，并输出更紧凑稳定的 fdata。
learning_goals: 理解 perf2bolt 模式（AggregateOnly）与 brstack/LBR 的关系
掌握 DataAggregator 解析 perf.data 的流程
理解聚合后 fdata 为何更稳定（地址无关）
minimal_modules: 分支数据聚合与 fdata 输出
lectures.practice_task: 对照 tools/driver/llvm-bolt.cpp 的 perf2boltMode()，说明 AggregateOnly/ShowDensity 如何被设置；在 DataAggregator 中找到 checkPerfDataMagic，解释为什么可以直接把 perf.data 喂给 llvm-bolt（-p）而跳过 perf2bolt。

lectures.title: Bolt Address Translation（BAT）：从优化后二进制回采 profile
lectures.topic: 讲清 BAT 机制：BOLT 在输出二进制中插入 .note.bolt_bat，记录地址翻译表，使后续能从 BOLT 优化过的二进制采集 profile 并映射回原始输入二进制再次优化。
learning_goals: 理解 BAT 解决的痛点（迭代优化的 profile 采集）
掌握 .note.bolt_bat section 的结构与用途
理解 --enable-bat 与 perf2bolt 的配合
minimal_modules: BAT section 结构（热/冷函数表）
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 docs/BAT.md，用一段话解释为什么没有 BAT 就很难对已优化的二进制再次迭代优化；用 bat-dump 工具的源码（tools/bat-dump/bat-dump.cpp）说明如何读取并展示 BAT section。

lectures.title: Heatmap 可视化与 Stale Profile Matching
lectures.topic: 讲清两个 profile 相关能力：Heatmap 工具/类把 profile 密度可视化为热点地图；StaleProfileMatching 在二进制与采集时已不一致（stale）时尽量匹配 profile。

掌握 stale profile 的成因与 StaleProfileMatching 的匹配思路
会用 heatmap 工具与 -dyno-stats 评估 profile 质量
lectures.practice_task: 用 heatmap 工具（参照 docs/Heatmaps.md）对一个带 profile 的二进制生成热点图，并解释横纵坐标的含义；阅读 StaleProfileMatching.cpp 的入口，说明它在什么情况下被触发、用什么策略匹配旧 profile。

units.title: Pass 框架：注册、顺序、并行与统计

lectures.title: BinaryFunctionPassManager：pass 框架、顺序与并行
lectures.topic: 讲清 BOLT 的 pass 基础设施：BinaryFunctionPass 基类、registerPass/runAllPasses 的注册与顺序、runOnFunctions 的并行执行（ParallelUtilities）、DynoStats 与 VerifyCFG。
learning_goals: 掌握 BinaryFunctionPass 基类与 runOnFunctions 接口
理解 runAllPasses 中 pass 的注册顺序即执行顺序
理解 ParallelUtilities 如何并行、DynoStats/VerifyCFG 如何校验
lectures.practice_task: 在 BinaryPassManager.cpp 的 runPasses() 中，说明 pass 是否执行取决于注册时的哪个布尔参数；并解释 ParallelUtilities::runOnEachFunctionWithUniqueAllocId 在 disassembleFunctions 中如何避免多线程 MCPlus allocator 冲突。

lectures.title: 基础整理 pass：从 NormalizeCFG 到 FinalizeFunctions
lectures.topic: 挑出贯穿管线的基础 pass 讲清它们的作用：NormalizeCFG、ShortenInstructions、RemoveNops、FixupBranches、AssignSections、FinalizeFunctions、InstructionLowering 等。
learning_goals: 理解 NormalizeCFG 如何规整 CFG 以便后续优化
掌握 FixupBranches 与 FinalizeFunctions 为何要在布局确定后运行
理解 InstructionLowering 把伪指令落地为真实指令的时机
lectures.practice_task: 在 runAllPasses() 中找出注释里强调'必须最后运行'或'依赖最终布局'的 pass（如 FinalizeFunctions、FixupBranches、CleanMCState），各写一句话说明它们为什么必须在那个位置。

lectures.title: Identical Code Folding（ICF）：折叠相同函数体
lectures.topic: 讲清 ICF 如何检测字节级/语义级相同的函数并折叠为一个，以减少代码体积；并说明它在管线中运行两次的原因。
learning_goals: 理解 ICF 检测相同函数的原理与安全条件
掌握 ICF level 选项与正确性约束
理解为何 ICF 在 Inliner 前后各运行一次
minimal_modules: ICF level 与安全性（hash/语义）
管线中两次 ICF 的位置
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 IdenticalCodeFolding.cpp 的入口，说明它用什么粒度（指令序列/重定位/符号）判定两个函数相同；并在 runAllPasses() 中找出 ICF 的两次注册位置，解释为什么 Inliner 之后需要再跑一次。

units.title: 核心优化 pass：布局、分裂与调用优化

lectures.title: 基本块排序与 Ext-TSP 布局算法

learning_goals: 掌握 ClusterAlgorithm 与 ReorderAlgorithm 的类层次
理解 Ext-TSP 评分模型（fall-through、跳转距离、缓存密度）
理解 -reorder-blocks 各取值如何选择算法
lectures.practice_task: 在 ReorderAlgorithm.h 中列出 ReorderAlgorithm 的所有子类与对应 Cluster 算法；阅读 ExtTSPReorderAlgorithm，用一段话解释它的评分函数如何同时考虑 fall-through 命中率与跳转距离，并说明 ext-tsp 为何是默认选项。

lectures.title: 函数排序：HFSort、Pettis-Hansen、CDSort 与 MCF

掌握 HFSort/Pettis-Hansen/CDSort 的差异与 -reorder-functions 选项
理解 CallGraph、CallGraphWalker 与 MCF 的角色

lectures.title: SplitFunctions：热冷分裂与 cdsplit
lectures.topic: 讲清 SplitFunctions 如何把函数的冷基本块拆到独立 .text.cold section，以及为何在 ReorderFunctions 之后会第二次运行（支持 hot-warm-cold 的 cdsplit 策略）。
learning_goals: 掌握热冷分裂的收益（提升指令缓存局部性）
理解 FunctionFragment 与分裂的判定阈值
理解管线中两次 SplitFunctions 的不同目的
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 SplitFunctions.cpp 的核心逻辑，说明如何根据执行计数判定一个基本块是否冷；在 runAllPasses() 中找到两次 SplitFunctions 注册，解释为什么第二次要在 ReorderFunctions 之后（参考源码注释）。

lectures.title: 调用相关优化：ICP、Inliner、SCTC 与 PLT
lectures.topic: 讲清几个直接改造调用图的 pass：IndirectCallPromotion（ICP，热点间接调用转直接）、Inliner、SimplifyConditionalTailCalls（SCTC，条件尾调用转跳转）、PLTCall。
learning_goals: 理解 ICP 如何用 profile 把热点间接调用转成直接调用梯子
掌握 BOLT 二进制级 inlining 的特点与限制
理解 SCTC 如何消除条件尾调用的冗余跳转

lectures.title: 栈帧与寄存器优化：FrameOptimizer、RegReAssign、ShrinkWrapping
lectures.topic: 讲清依赖数据流分析的进阶 pass：FrameOptimizer（利用栈帧分析省去存取）、RegReAssign（重分配寄存器）、ShrinkWrapping（收缩 prologue/epilogue 范围），以及它们依赖的 FrameAnalysis/LivenessAnalysis。
learning_goals: 理解 FrameOptimizer 依赖的栈帧数据流分析
掌握 RegReAssign 如何用 profile 重新分配寄存器
理解 ShrinkWrapping 收缩 prologue/epilogue 的收益与风险
lectures.practice_task: 在 runAllPasses() 中找到 FrameOptimizerPass 并阅读注释，解释它为何必须依赖 FinalizeFunctions（需要正确放置 CFI）；列出它读取/改写 CFI 所需的栈帧分析来自哪个 pass。

理解 X86/AArch64/RISCV 三个实现的差异（如 LongJmp 放松）
理解新增后端的步骤与必须先落地的公共改动

lectures.topic: 讲清 emitAndLink 阶段：BinaryEmitter 用 MCStreamer 把优化后的函数重新发射为可链接对象，JITLinkLinker 基于 LLVM ORC 把它链接回内存以得到最终地址。

lectures.title: 运行时库与插桩：RuntimeLibrary、Instrumentation 与 Hugify

理解 runtime/ 为何要 freestanding（-ffreestanding，无 BSS/无依赖）
